newsitem.title: GERMANY: Brau und Brunnen to revamp to reach profit.
newsitem.headline: Brau und Brunnen to revamp to reach profit.

text.p: German brewing and drinks group Brau und Brunnen AG said on Friday it would rationalise, shed capacity, and streamline its portfolio of beer brands to cut debt and return to profit.
The group would make unspecified operating losses in 1996 and 1997 but aimed to become profitable again in 1998, it said in a mandatory statement released early on Friday.
It also aimed to halve its debt of 850 million marks in the medium term, but did not specify a time frame.
Brau und Brunnen will sell real estate to cover operating losses and finance a planned restructuring of its drinks business, the statement said.

It had not yet decided which subsidiaries to sell, apart from data processing unit Brau und Brunnen Informatik Service GmbH, and said concrete steps would be discussed at a supervisory board meeting on February 13.
Drinks sales were expected to fall about eight percent to 15.4 million hectolitres in 1996, or by four percent if adjusted for the sale of subsidiaries.
The group's workforce will shrink by nine percent to about 4,500 people by the end of 1996 compared with 1995.
On Thursday, Bavarian bank Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG said it would buy an additional 24.8 percent of Brau und Brunnen this year, raising its holding to a majority stake.
The bank said it planned to sell the 24.8 percent stake eventually.
